context:
Goal: model calls from hooks work on every account and device, or ask once for setup (your words, 11:43 CST Nov 6).
Problem (rule): you said "An API key is an option, not the first route", but a standing decision keeps the API key out of the hook judge's process, so an account with only an API key gets a setup-token message and never a working judge.
Based on (ruling): your Nov 6 11:43 CST words on model-call setup, quoted above.
Based on (read): only code keeps ANTHROPIC_API_KEY out of the judge's process: the allow list and its comment in hooks/decision_watch.py. Corrected 11:40 CST Nov 12: no decision record says so. The nearest record, decision mods-no-cli-key-headless (how mods run with no command-line key), names a stored API token as the fallback if the mod route fails, which leans toward b.
Departs from: main's setup message for an account with only an API key — a rewrites it to name `claude setup-token` and say the key route is not offered for hook judges; b instead passes the key to the judge when no token exists.
Meanwhile: the lane rebuilding the model-call setup check builds option a.

lastAnswer.note: we can make it a network secret and/or store the key somewhere that keeps it hidden but still callable im open to ideas if you're worried about key safety

options.gain: The standing decision holds, and no hook's child process ever sees the API key.
options.how: The setup message tells the account to run `claude setup-token` and says the API key route is not offered for hook judges.
options.label: Keep the key out; the message says so (Recommended)
options.lose: An account with only an API key has no working hook judge.

options.gain: Accounts with only an API key get a working hook judge.
options.how: The judge's process gets ANTHROPIC_API_KEY only when no setup-token file exists.
options.label: Pass the key only when no token exists
options.lose: A hook's child process can see the API key, which reverses the standing decision for the judge.

ref: step model-call-auth-check; decision mods-no-cli-key-headless; hooks/decision_watch.py JUDGE_ENV_ALLOWLIST; lane fan-prose-unmapped-3 (session_013NEJL1CWKBkSQYFqekzCnf)
reply: Recorded 12:00 CST: the judge gets the API key when no setup token exists. The lane was building a, so the coordinator re-points it to b. Key storage: the lane proposes a hidden store (environment secret in the cloud, the system keychain on your computers) and brings it back if it needs a pick.
title: Should a hook's model judge use an API key when the account has no setup token?
why: Recommended: a. It keeps the API key away from hook processes, and the lane is already building it.
